name: Anterior thalamic nuclei (ATN) excitatory projection neuron
morphology_summary: Thalamocortical relay-cell plan shared by all ATN projection types: few primary dendrites (3.8 +/- 0.1), no local axon, elaborate tufted spiny distal dendrites (Hintiryan et al., 2025)
ephys_summary: No direct intrinsic ephys reported; Olig3-lineage nuclei generally show driver-like thalamocortical properties (review inference, Clasca et al., 2012). AD/AV contain head-direction cells
connectivity_summary: Papez-circuit node: inputs from mammillary bodies (mammillothalamic tract) and subicular complex (fornix and nonfornical route); reciprocal with retrosplenial, presubicular and cingulate cortex; afferents largely nucleus-specific with little collateralization
development_summary: Born E10.5-E16.5 in dorsal thalamic glutamatergic lineage (Gbx2+, likely Olig3 lineage); early-differentiating Sox2+ / Cadm1+ branch (Govek et al., 2022); not Dlx interneuron lineage
subtypes_noted: Report frames three discrete nucleus-matched glutamatergic classes AD, AV, AM (Kapustina et al., 2024), each with dorsomedial-ventrolateral gradients, and a 13-type projection-defined scheme nested within them (Hintiryan et al., 2025): AD1-2, AV1-3, AM1-3, ADP, AMd, AMv, AMdc, AMV
split_rationale: The report explicitly treats AD, AV and AM excitatory neurons as distinct types: separate sections per nucleus with distinct inputs (lateral mammillary + para/postsubiculum -> AD; medial mammillary + presubiculum/distal subiculum -> AV; medial mammillary + proximal subiculum -> AM), distinct cortical output biases (retrosplenial/postsubicular vs granular RSC L1 vs anterior cingulate/frontal), distinct transcript markers (Pvalb, Htr2a for AD; C1ql2, Bdnf, Grp_KH288-Cre subset for AV; Rspo2, Tnnt1 for AM), and an explicit working model in which 'discrete nucleus-level glutamatergic classes: AD, AV, AM' are recovered as three discrete scRNA-seq/spatial clusters (Kapustina et al., 2024). The ATN node is retained as the shared parent (common glutamatergic relay-cell scaffold, morphology, Papez circuit placement), and AD/AV/AM are proposed as child types. The finer 13 Hintiryan projection-defined types are recorded only under subtypes_noted on each child, not proposed as separate nodes: they come from a single study, lack one-to-one marker resolution (AM1 has no marker; AD1/AD2 and AV1-3 lack unique markers) and are not mapped to transcriptomic states.
quote_count_note: All 171 extracted quote entries (45 sources) concern ATN excitatory neurons; per-nucleus counts below are keyword-matched and overlap

name: Anterodorsal thalamic nucleus (AD) excitatory projection neuron
negative_markers_mentioned: Grp_KH288-Cre (transgene; labels AV subset, none in AD)
morphology_summary: Shared ATN relay-cell morphology; AD1 and AD2 differ in local morphology and topology (Hintiryan et al., 2025). Up to ~15% of labelled AD cells bifurcate to different retrosplenial areas (rat; Yanakieva et al., 2022)
ephys_summary: Head-direction cells most prominent in AD (Taube, 1995; Aggleton et al., 2015); no intrinsic ephys reported
connectivity_summary: Inputs: bilateral lateral mammillary (head-direction system), para/postsubiculum via nonfornical internal capsule route. Outputs: retrosplenial cortex, postsubiculum/presubiculum (reciprocal), visual areas, mammillary regions, moderate/limited ACC area 24a; strong drive onto RSG L3 low-rheobase neurons
subtypes_noted: AD1 (dorsolateral AD; projects to postsubiculum, LD/LI visual areas, mammillary regions) and AD2 (ventromedial AD; projects to retrosplenial, visual, postsubicular, mammillary regions) (Hintiryan et al., 2025); no marker separating AD1 from AD2

name: Anteroventral thalamic nucleus (AV) excitatory projection neuron
morphology_summary: Shared ATN relay-cell morphology; axons to granular RSC heterogeneous: type 1 arborizing only in layer Ia, type 2 also branching in layers III/IV (rat single-axon; Odagiri et al., 2011)
ephys_summary: Contains some head-direction cells (less than AD); no intrinsic ephys reported
connectivity_summary: Inputs: ipsilateral medial mammillary (pars lateralis), presubiculum and distal dorsal subiculum (mostly fornix; postsubicular input to lateral dorsal AV nonfornical), lighter ACC input to AVDM, MCC/PCC input to AVVL/AVDM. Outputs: major thalamic source to granular RSC layer 1 (L1a), plus ACC, secondary motor, entorhinal cortex
subtypes_noted: AV1 (dorsomedial; prelimbic, ACC, anterior RSC), AV2 (ventrolateral; granular RSC, ventral visual stream), AV3 (dorsolateral; prefrontal + visual) (Hintiryan et al., 2025); dorsomedial-ventrolateral transcript gradient covarying with protein and inputs (Kapustina et al., 2024)

name: Anteromedial thalamic nucleus (AM) excitatory projection neuron
morphology_summary: Shared ATN relay-cell morphology; AM types differ in local morphology and topology; only principal ATN nucleus with modest bifurcating neurons reaching ACC plus prefrontal or retrosplenial cortex (Yanakieva et al., 2022)
connectivity_summary: Inputs: ipsilateral medial mammillary (pars medialis; earliest mammillothalamic target developmentally), proximal subiculum almost exclusively via fornix, heavy ACC/MCC input. Outputs: anterior cingulate (areas 24a/24b), prelimbic, secondary motor, entorhinal, retrosplenial cortex; contributes input to callosal OPCs under MOs
subtypes_noted: At least eight projection-defined types (Hintiryan et al., 2025): AM1 (throughout; cingulate + RSC; no marker), AM2 (ventrolateral; prefrontal, prostriata, ventral visual), AM3 (throughout; Tnnt1+; prefrontal, cingulate, RSC), ADP (dorsal posterior AM; Cacna2d1+), AMd, AMv, AMdc (dorsal cap; Tnnt1+), AMV (ventral border; Col5a1+; ventral orbital, agranular insular, entorhinal); Calb1 marks another broadly distributed AM type
